question: A 57-year-old man comes to his office seeking information about the surgical treatment of lower urinary tract symptoms secondary to prostate growth. You have to give him advice about it. Which of the following messages is true?

options.opa: Among the absolute indications for surgery for symptoms of the lower urinary tract secondary to prostate growth are recurrent urinary tract infections, bladder lithiasis and recurrent hematuria.
options.opb: Prostatic stents are a very interesting minimally invasive treatment option for young men with low symptoms of the lower urinary tract secondary to prostate growth.
options.opc: The patient surgically treated for symptoms of the lower urinary tract secondary to prostate growth requires a very thorough follow-up, with controls every three months during the first year and every six months thereafter.
options.opd: Unfortunately, erectile dysfunction is the norm after surgical treatment for symptoms of the lower urinary tract secondary to prostatic growth.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Surgical treatment for lower urinary tract symptoms secondary to prostate growth may be indicated for conditions like recurrent urinary tract infections, bladder lithiasis, and recurrent hematuria -> These are considered absolute indications for surgery -> 80%

CHAIN: Prostatic stents are a minimally invasive treatment option for lower urinary tract symptoms secondary to prostate growth -> Prostatic stents may be suitable for certain cases, but not typically recommended for young men with low symptoms -> 70%

CHAIN: Patients undergoing surgical treatment for lower urinary tract symptoms secondary to prostate growth require thorough follow-up -> Follow-up typically includes controls every three months during the first year and every six months thereafter -> 85%

CHAIN: Erectile dysfunction can be a common complication after surgical treatment for lower urinary tract symptoms secondary to prostatic growth -> Erectile dysfunction may occur due to surgical intervention affecting nerve function or blood flow to the penis -> 90%
analysis: Surgical treatment for lower urinary tract symptoms secondary to prostate growth is a viable option in certain cases. It is important to provide accurate information to the patient to help them make an informed decision.
